newsitem.title: CHINA: PRESS DIGEST - Chinese newspapers - Oct 3.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Chinese newspapers - Oct 3.

text.p: Following is a summary of major Chinese political and business stories in leading newspapers, prepared by Reuters in Beijing. Reuters has not checked the stories and does not guarantee their accuracy. Telephone: (8610) 6532-1921. Fax: (8610) 6532-4978.
President Jiang Zemin, in a visit to People's Daily, calls for greater efforts in correctly guiding public opinion.
A children's book fair opens in Beijing and a commentary calls for more and better publications to provide spiritual nourishment for children.
Central bank governor Dai Xianglong, speaking in Hong Kong, says China's foreign exchange reserves are to hit $95 billion by the end of 1996.
A commentary urges Sinopec to compete with foreign companies such as Shell and Mobil.
China National Petroleum Corp is to invest 4.3 billion yuan in a natural gas and fertiliser project in the northwestern Xinjiang region.
Economists urge China to set up an economic zone on the Qinghai-Tibet plateau to boost overall economic development there.
